blocks.alt: Van Lettering and Decals in Toronto How DJW Masonry Branded Their GMC Savana

blocks.html:
Van Lettering and Decals in Toronto give growing trade businesses an affordable, high-impact way to turn a plain work vehicle into a rolling billboard — and that is exactly what we delivered for DJW Masonry & Restoration on their GMC Savana cargo van. The client arrived with a clean white van carrying nothing more than a small contact panel. They left with a sharp, professional decal layout that puts their full service list, logo, contact details and a scannable QR code in front of every driver, homeowner and property manager they pass across the GTA.

At Vinyl Wrap Toronto, this is one of the most requested jobs we do for masonry, restoration and construction crews — and one of the best-value branding moves a small business can make.

From Plain White Van to Mobile Billboard

The “before” was typical of most working vans: a white GMC Savana with a single magnetic-style sign on the driver’s door and very little else. Functional, but easy to forget.

The “after” tells a completely different story. We designed and installed a full driver-side decal package that includes:

  • The DJW Masonry & Restoration wordmark and hexagonal “D” logo
  • A clean, two-column service list — Brickwork, Stonework, Chimney Repairs, Tuckpointing, Parging and Historic Restoration
  • A “Free Estimates” call-out with email and phone number
  • A scannable QR code that links directly to the business
  • Partner badges, including the Flexstone Coatings logo

The result is balanced, readable and unmistakably professional — a van that looks like it belongs to an established company rather than a side hustle.

Why DJW Masonry Chose Lettering and Decals Over a Full Wrap

For trades like masonry and restoration, a full colour-change wrap is often overkill. Crews keep their vehicles white or factory colour, and what they really need is clear, legible information that generates phone calls.

That is where commercial van decals win:

  • Lower cost than a full or partial wrap, with most of the marketing impact
  • Faster turnaround — usually a day rather than several
  • Easy to update when a phone number, service or partner changes
  • Clean, corporate look that reads instantly at a red light or job site

Vehicle graphics remain one of the most cost-effective forms of advertising available. A single branded van working across the GTA can generate tens of thousands of daily impressions for a one-time cost — no monthly ad spend required. For a masonry company driving between Etobicoke, Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Vaughan job sites every week, that exposure adds up fast.

What Goes Into a Professional Van Decal Job

Good decals are not just stickers slapped on a panel. Here is how we approached the DJW Masonry project.

Our Process

  1. Design & layout. Our in-house design team mapped the service list, logo and contact block to the flat panel of the Savana so everything stays readable at highway speed and clear of body lines, rivets and the fuel door.
  2. Proof & approval. The client reviewed a digital mock-up before anything was printed or cut.
  3. Surface prep. The panel is cleaned and de-greased so the vinyl bonds properly — a step many DIY jobs skip, and the main reason cheap decals peel.
  4. Precision installation. Certified installers apply cut lettering and printed decals with proper alignment, squeegee technique and heat where needed.

Materials We Used

This job combines cut vinyl lettering for the text with printed decals for the logo, QR code and partner badges. We build these jobs with premium films from 3M and Avery Dennison, which are engineered specifically for commercial fleet graphics and Canadian weather. You can read more about 3M’s commercial vehicle graphic films on the official 3M Graphics site.

Every job is backed by our 3-year warranty against peeling, bubbling and fading.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

After hundreds of van lettering and decal jobs, here are the errors we see most often:

  • Cramming in too much text. If a driver can’t read it in three seconds, it isn’t working. Lead with your name, service and phone number.
  • Using low-grade vinyl. Economy film fades and lifts within a season of Ontario winters. Cast films from 3M and Avery Dennison last for years.
  • Skipping surface prep. Dirt, wax or road salt under the vinyl guarantees early failure.
  • Forgetting a call to action. A QR code or “Free Estimates” line — like DJW’s — turns a glance into a lead.

Brand Your Fleet Across the GTA

Van Lettering and Decals in Toronto remain the smartest first branding investment for masonry, restoration and contracting businesses — high visibility, low cost and built to last. DJW Masonry & Restoration now has a GMC Savana that markets the company on every drive, whether it’s parked on a residential street in Etobicoke or heading out to a job in Vaughan.

If you run a trade business anywhere in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan or across Ontario, we can help you do the same. Our certified installers, in-house design team and fast turnaround make professional branding simple.

  1. What is the difference between van lettering and a van wrap?

    Van lettering uses cut vinyl text and spot decals applied directly to the factory panel, while a wrap covers large areas or the whole vehicle. Lettering and decals are the most affordable option and ideal for trade businesses that want clear contact info without changing the vehicle’s colour.

  2. How long do commercial van decals last?

    With premium 3M or Avery Dennison cast films and proper installation, quality decals typically last 5 to 7 years. At Vinyl Wrap Toronto, every job is backed by a 3-year warranty against peeling, bubbling and fading.

  3. Will decals damage my van’s paint?

    No. When professionally installed on factory paint in good condition and removed correctly with heat, vinyl decals come off cleanly without harming the finish — and can even protect the paint underneath.

  4. How much do van decals cost in Toronto?

    Basic lettering starts around $250–$450, while a full decal package with both sides, rear doors and printed graphics can range from $900 to $1,800. Exact pricing depends on coverage and design, so we provide free estimates.

  5. How long does installation take?

    Most lettering and decal jobs are completed within a single day once the design is approved. Larger or printed packages may take slightly longer.

  6. Can I include a QR code on my van like DJW Masonry did?

    Yes. A QR code is one of the best additions to commercial van decals — it lets people instantly visit your website, request a quote or save your contact details from their phone.

  7. Do you service businesses outside Etobicoke?

    Absolutely. We’re based in Etobicoke and serve clients across Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan and the wider GTA and Ontario.
